newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-KALLIS CENTURY SEES MIDDLESEX TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KALLIS CENTURY SEES MIDDLESEX TRIUMPH.

text.p: A century from South African Jacques Kallis boosted Middlesex to a thrilling four-wicket NatWest Trophy win over Gloucestershire with just three balls to spare at Uxbridge on Wednesday.
West Indian Monte Lynch earlier led Gloucestershire to 277 for nine, hitting exactly 100 in just 108 balls and with nine fours and two sixes.
But then Kallis, who was also Middlesex's leading wicket-taker with four for 47, weighed in with exactly 100 of his own off 138 deliveries with three sixes and six fours.
Then Jason Pooley, hitting his first half-century in the competition, cracked an unbeaten 79 and hit a boundary off the third ball of the final over to enable Middlesex to win by four wickets.
Australian Stuart Law was another to score exactly 100 as he steered Essex to a seven-wicket victory over Worcestershire at Chelmsford in another second round match.
His 91-ball innings laid the foundation for victory with 15 balls to spare after Graeme Hick's 146 had been the mainstay of the visitors' 286 for nine.

Law helped himself to two sixes and 11 fours before he was finally caught in the deep after sharing in a third-wicket stand of 132 in 24 overs with Ronnie Irani. But then Irani (79 not out)and Paul Grayson (82 not out) shared an unbroken stand of 136 in 29 overs to complete a comfortable win.

Hick had needed just 157 deliveries to score his runs, 26 of which came in one over from left-arm spinner Grayson. In all, he plundered 10 fours and five sixes, one of which left a women spectator needing attention after being struck above an eye.
Former Warwickshire skipper Dermot Reeve made an unhappy return to Edgbaston as his former charges pulled off the kind of miraculous win he often masterminded to dump Somerset out of the competition.
Reeve won the NatWest Trophy on four occasions, once with Sussex and three times with Warwickshire, before moving to Taunton as coach at the end of last season.
But there will be no Lord's trip for him this September after his side surrendered a position of strength when chasing a target of 221 in 60 overs.

They reached 135 for two and needed only 86 from the final 20 overs with eight wickets in hand, but were then undone by inspired spells from pacemen Gladstone Small and South African Allan Donald who each took three wickets.
Spinner Ashley Giles wrapped up the game by bowling last-man Andy Caddick with nine balls remaining as Warwickshire squeezed home by 11 runs.
Fast bowler Devon Malcolm fired Derbyshire past Northamptonshire and into the quarter-finals with a seven-wicket burst, and then said he was itching to get back into the England fold.

The 34 year old paceman, omitted from the squad defeated in the third test, claimed competition-best figures of seven for 35 from 10.1 overs as Northants were shot out for 180, chasing a mammoth 324 for seven.
